name: Harden and package for daily personal use
summary: Turn the existing labwc runtime into a supported, repeatedly used Linux alpha before expanding its tool surface.
value: Highest near-term value for the stated success criterion: fewer interruptions, predictable setup, trustworthy cleanup and real evidence of usefulness (F001, F007, F028).
cost: M overall: roughly several focused engineering weeks plus a two-week use diary; estimate, not a measured schedule.
risks: Real workflows may reveal application-specific fragility.
Maintaining a private wlroots repair can dominate packaging work.
A personal tool may remain valuable without attracting broad adoption.
prerequisites: User chooses two or three recurring workflows and first supported non-Nix distro.
Fix profile deletion, wait semantics, observation and responsiveness defects.
Agree on a cooperative same-user trust boundary for the pilot.
confirming_evidence: Fresh NixOS and non-Nix installs succeed from exact documented commands.
At least 20 real-work sessions over at least 10 working days record outputs, interventions and cleanup.
No unexplained wrong-target actions; zero owned-process leaks in declared supported failure cases.
Eight-hour soak remains responsive with bounded retained bytes.

name: Deepen agent interaction and semantic capabilities
summary: Optimize target-specific observation, semantic actions, verified outcomes and tool efficiency for recurring difficult applications.
value: Could reduce observation cost and wrong actions if actual failures are caused by the interface rather than model reasoning or setup (F004, F005, F008, F029).
cost: M–L: per-toolkit investigation, robust target identities, latency budgets and separately authorized model experiments.
risks: Large accessibility trees stall or exceed response limits.
Reduced tool calls can hide more primitive actions and higher token costs.
Custom-drawn/Electron/office interfaces may need different fallbacks.
More fixtures can remain saturated without improving real work.
prerequisites: O1 pilot identifies recurring interaction failures.
Bound traversal and repair target/observation semantics.
Pinned paired benchmark protocol and explicit paid-run budget.
confirming_evidence: Same real tasks fail with current tools and pass with the targeted extension.
Randomized paired trials on identical environments show fewer interventions or lower end-to-end cost without worse completion.
Report distributions, failures and cache counters, not only aggregate calls.

name: Add an explicit security and permissions boundary
summary: Place the desktop and applications inside an existing container or VM boundary with deliberate mounts, network and credential policies.
value: Useful if the agent handles untrusted apps/pages or the user expects takeover secrets to be hidden from a shell-capable agent (F002, F014, F024, F025).
cost: L: threat model, IPC/services, credential handling, mounts, network policy, packaging and adversarial validation.
risks: A policy UI can imply guarantees the underlying same-user process model cannot enforce.
Desktop integration, portals and GPU/audio support become harder.
Credential/session reuse conflicts with strict isolation.
Container and VM guarantees differ and need independent validation.
prerequisites: User states which actor is untrusted and what data must be protected.
Select existing containment primitives rather than inventing isolation.
Define explicit host bridges and allowed external effects.
confirming_evidence: Host files, credential sources, sockets and forbidden network routes remain inaccessible in controlled negative tests.
Takeover blocks all authorized observation channels in the defined threat model.
Crash cleanup and profile recovery work within the selected process boundary.
Useful workflows remain practical without broad host mounts.

name: Build a portable agent machine
summary: Implement prompt2's managed Linux environment behind Linux/Windows/macOS entry points, reusing this runtime inside it.
value: Could make setup reproducible and reach non-Linux users while retaining one Linux application environment (F030, F033).
cost: L, likely a multi-month platform effort: image updates, VM/WSL lifecycle, host bridge, repository storage/sync, viewer and support.
risks: Direct overlap with Cua and other provisioned environments.
Host filesystem watching, build performance and credentials may be worse than native.
Linux tasks do not validate native Windows/macOS behavior.
Reproducible packages do not imply deterministic app state or reversible external actions.
prerequisites: O1 proves recurring value and the user chooses cross-platform product scope.
Compare existing provisioning platforms before implementing a manager.
Choose WSL/container/VM by measured requirements and available target hardware.
confirming_evidence: One non-Linux host completes the same selected workflow from a fresh install.
Measured cold/warm startup, image size, repository I/O and update/rollback behavior meet user-agreed targets.
A small external pilot uses it repeatedly rather than only completing a demo.

name: Integrate or contribute to an existing runtime
summary: Keep the useful tests and adapters, and use or extend wbox, kde-mcp, Cua or E2B where a real comparison shows a lower maintenance path.
value: Potentially avoids owning provisioning, protocol and patch maintenance while preserving the original user outcome (F019, F031–F034).
cost: S for a tightly scoped evaluation, M–L if migration or upstream integration is justified.
risks: Documented capabilities may fail on NixOS or the actual workflow.
Licensing, trust boundaries and dependency footprint may differ.
Migration can lose lifecycle or session-routing properties already tested here.
prerequisites: Select one comparator for the chosen workflow and pin its revision.
Check component-level licensing and required host changes.
Use disposable state; no personal profiles or paid calls without scoped authorization.
confirming_evidence: The same installation-to-cleanup workflow is easier and at least as dependable.
Documented maintenance obligations are lower after accounting for adapters and upstream dependencies.
